static_traits.name: Wesley
static_traits.family_status: Father was a Communist Party member
static_traits.social_status: Have friends to talk to, but have not yet discussed this matter with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological issues in the past, no history of psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe emotions and experiences concretely; negative emotional tone; tendency toward catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, mental filtering and negating the positive; fairly cooperative, willing to try small steps.

basic_info.main_problem: After receiving negative feedback at a recent comedy performance, persistently feels a sense of failure and disappointment, and regards that performance as 'a complete disaster'.
basic_info.core_demands: Hopes to resolve the failure and disappointment persisting after that comedy performance.

core_beliefs: My value depends on others' evaluations

special_situations.event: In a comedy show with a full house, a few audience members booed, the overall reaction was lukewarm, and afterward someone bluntly commented 'you are not funny'.
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If some audience members express dissatisfaction or have not laughed, it proves I am a failure as a comedy Actor.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly ruminate on performance details, try to soothe myself with rationalized Interpretation, and imagine I must redeem myself through the next 'successful show'.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This performance was a total disaster.

special_situations.event: Whenever recalling that performance or thinking of performing on stage again.
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot make most people laugh, it means I am completely not good enough, and continuing to try has no meaning.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses 'wait until completely successful to speak' as the standard to postpone action, setting a perfectionist threshold before allowing herself to feel better.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I did not make everyone laugh this time, trying again has no meaning.

special_situations.event: In the same show there was also an audience member smiling and encouraging 'keep it up'.
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If someone in the audience genuinely finds it funny, it means I am not a completely worthless comedian.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proactively ignores or devalues positive information, focusing attention on negative evaluation to 'prove' their own failure.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Maybe this time was not a complete failure, I still have room to improve.

special_situations.event: When receiving feedback from others in later work or life (especially critical feedback).
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Audience laughter and applause are the standard for judging whether a comedian is not yet outdated.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Belittles herself in advance in her mind to lessen the blow of future setbacks; remains excessively vigilant about others' evaluations.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am actually not bad/a failure, I just still need to hone my craft.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized by the audience and others, proving I am an 'interesting and valuable' person
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being negated, worry about losing the audience, fear of staying in place without growth
defense_goal: Use Intellectualization to mask the pain brought by Self-deprecation in order to negate vulnerability
Avoid discussing the true feeling of 'not loving' comedy as a career, maintaining the image of a 'professional comedian'

object_relations.object_representation: Picky, harsh, and judgmental audiences / others
An audience that does not understand and may laugh at me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When recalling that performance or facing others' feedback on one's work
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Over-identify with the audience's immediate reaction, negate 'not funny' (removing the fact that 'someone found it funny / someone applauded' from identification)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Speaks in an analytical, evidence-listing manner, tone flat, avoiding expressing emotions such as shame and sadness.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking about confiding this setback experience to a friend
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Preset 'a comedian not being booed' as the equation 'Projection: failure is shameful'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Encourage distinguishing 'comedian' as a professional identity from 'not funny' as a single-show evaluation, avoiding generalizing a single failure into identity negation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing whether to continue performing or how to improve
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously treat 'being booed' as evidence of 'failure', without realizing situational factors
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use'a normalizing statement: people say Meaninglessness things under pressure' to reduce self-blame.

manifestations: When not yet realizing audience reactions are influenced by many factors, fall into self-blame
Negative feedback looms like a dark cloud, hard to detach from
outcomes: Decreased drive, declining motivation increases Anticipation
Low mood and Worsening sense of failure

manifestations: Treat a single failure as the ultimate judgment on the comedian identity, have not seen the situational factors

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Repeated self-criticism (such as 'I must be terrible')
Over-identify with the audience's immediate reaction, ignoring long-term accumulation and negating evidence
In sessions, tends to emphasize failures and ignore the positive side

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Treat 'a comedian not being booed' as 'failure', ignoring the inherent uncertainty of the comedy career

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Treats the external standard of 'must make everyone laugh to count as success' as a self-demand
Habitual negation and self-blame without recognizing situational factors

exception_events.target_problem: When recalling that performance or facing feedback from others, the client usually focuses only on the negative evaluations, quickly reaches the conclusion 'I am terrible / the performance was a disaster', and falls into a sense of failure and disappointment.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In a small show, although there was only scattered laughter, the audience's applause made me feel recognized, and at the time I did not engage in Self-denial like now, showing that 'not funny' is not absolute.
exception_events.reason: not every show gets booed; not every comedian gets questioned: when performing in small shows or in front of acquaintances, I have felt recognized, and have had moments remembered for improvisation.

positive_force: Through Reflection see the negate mechanism behind the pain (e.g. the equation 'being booed = failure'), beginning to question its rationality
Having friend resources to turn to for help
Can also notice positive feedback in the same event
Anxiety about work not yet starting (Work not yet started)
negative_force: Doubting the comedy career, ignoring accumulated experience, over-identifying with the audience's negation leads to self-negation.
Overly reliant on external evaluations to define self-worth
Repeatedly ruminates on negative events, attention occupied by the negative
When envisioning the future of the comedy career: 'Male' not 'a recognized comedian'
Declining motivation leads to Anticipation (feeling 'this time it will not work' and therefore not trying')

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly watch comedy performance videos, looking for points that make me laugh, for Self-denial
antecedent: Receiving others' feedback at work or in life
target_behavior.core_reason: Highly sensitive to negative evaluation, equates a few negative comments with overall failure, and ties self-worth to others' evaluations
target_behavior.function: Relieve self-doubt by revisiting comedy, seeking humorous Anxiety (envisioning Anxiety about the comedy career)
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, declining motivation leads to missed opportunities; ignoring positive feedback amid progress intensifies Self-denial

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding confiding in and seeking help from friends
antecedent: Thinking about telling friends about this setback
target_behavior.core_reason: Worry that the 'not good enough' comedian identity will be reinforced by the equation 'Projection: failure is shameful'
target_behavior.function: Avoid being laughed at through negation, maintaining fragile Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased support, Increased subjective sense of isolation, comedy career stagnates, falling into the 'no one understands' cycle
